title: I got a wrong number text asking me to leave the porch light off tonight. It knew my address.
story:
The message came at 8:15 PM. Please leave the porch light off tonight. It makes them restless.

I replied that it was a wrong number. The answer came in seconds. No. You're the right house.

I laughed it off and left the light on. Then my phone buzzed again. Please. You don't understand what's walking the street when it's lit.

I went outside. The street was normal. Sprinklers, parked cars, one dog barking far away. I flipped the switch off anyway, mostly to make the texts stop.

The dog stopped barking.

Another text. Thank you. Now stay inside and don't look at the window by the door.

I looked at the window by the door.

On the glass, from outside, was a small clean handprint, and it was fresh. It was at the height of my chest.

My phone buzzed one last time. This one wasn't from the stranger. It was from my own number.

It said, Turn the light back on. I've been standing here for an hour.

I haven't moved from the hallway.

The porch light is still off.
premise: wrong number warns to keep porch light off; final text arrives from the narrator's own number
